messages.content:
Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

Now perform the same with the following input
input: {
    "question": "user: What is the difference between vaccinating a minor and vaccinating a major?\nassistant: I am sorry that I do not have specific information comparing the process or implications of vaccinating minor versus major. \nuser:  COVID Vaccine Myths\nassistant: The FAQs about COVID Vaccine Myths document addresses several common misconceptions about the COVID-19 vaccine. Here are three key points from the document:\n1. COVID-19 vaccines do not interact with or change your DNA in any way.\n2. Receiving a COVID-19 vaccine will not make you magnetic as they do not contain ingredients that can produce an electromagnetic field.\n3. None of the COVID-19 vaccines authorized for use in the United States shed or release any of their components.\n\nuser: how does COVID-19 Vaccines work?",
    "answer": "COVID-19 vaccines work by presenting the immune system with a safe way to recognize the coronavirus’s spike protein. The Novavax vaccine injects the spike protein itself, while Pfizer and Moderna mRNA vaccines teach the body to make the spike protein, prompting an immune response. The body produces antibodies that help it recognize and fight the virus quickly if exposed again. The evidence also states that these vaccine methods cannot cause COVID-19. [S9] [S4] [S2]"
}
Output:

response_text:
{
  "statements": [
    "COVID-19 vaccines provide the immune system with a safe way to recognize the coronavirus spike protein.",
    "The Novavax vaccine introduces the coronavirus spike protein into the body.",
    "Pfizer and Moderna mRNA vaccines instruct the body to produce the coronavirus spike protein.",
    "The coronavirus spike protein produced after Pfizer or Moderna vaccination prompts an immune response.",
    "The body produces antibodies in response to COVID-19 vaccination.",
    "Antibodies help the body recognize and fight the coronavirus quickly during a subsequent exposure.",
    "The cited evidence states that the Novavax, Pfizer, and Moderna vaccine methods cannot cause COVID-19."
  ]
}

statements: COVID-19 vaccines provide the immune system with a safe way to recognize the coronavirus spike protein.
The Novavax vaccine introduces the coronavirus spike protein into the body.
Pfizer and Moderna mRNA vaccines instruct the body to produce the coronavirus spike protein.
The coronavirus spike protein produced after Pfizer or Moderna vaccination prompts an immune response.
The body produces antibodies in response to COVID-19 vaccination.
Antibodies help the body recognize and fight the coronavirus quickly during a subsequent exposure.
The cited evidence states that the Novavax, Pfizer, and Moderna vaccine methods cannot cause COVID-19.
